hero.title: Kiron Atom Tellian
hero.subtitle: Pianist · Composer
hero.imageAlt: Kiron Atom Tellian seated at a grand piano.

pressCycle.quote: Without resorting to ostentatious virtuosity, articulated phrases, accents, and lyrical lines with remarkable freedom.
…an incredible combination of sensitivity and taste.
The bravura and maturity of his playing render speechless.
One enters a state of weightlessness — following, as if suspended, by the whims of the wind blown by the performer.
Undoubtedly one of the greatest and most talented pianists from Austria.
One of the day's most interesting musicians, with an individual style that brought to mind some of the earlier Bach performances of Ivo Pogorelich.
Tellian's fingers flew about the keyboard, perfectly depicting the weightless elegance of the waltz.
What an allegro giusto! Their riveting performance was met with an incredibly long applause.
His ability to connect virtuosity and intimate sensitivity, explosive drama, longing and singing melodies was extraordinary.

bio: Austrian pianist and composer Kiron Atom Tellian is currently pursuing his bachelor’s degree at The Juilliard School in New York, studying with Maestro Sergei Babayan as a recipient of the prestigious Kovner Fellowship. Born in Vienna, he began his piano studies at the University for Music and Performing Arts Vienna (MDW) at age seven and made his orchestral debut at nine.

Tellian has garnered top prizes at international competitions across Europe, the USA, and Japan. In 2024, he won the YCA Susan Wadsworth International Auditions, receiving eight special prizes. As a composer, his works have been widely recognised; this season, he has been commissioned to write an orchestral work premiering at the Vienna Musikverein.

This season, Tellian performs at the Vienna Konzerthaus, the Viotti Festival, the Vienna Musikverein, and made his debut with the Orchestra Sinfonica di Milano in Chopin’s First Piano Concerto. Looking ahead: debuts with the San Diego Symphony, a recital at Villa Senar invited by the Rachmaninov Foundation, and his solo recital debut at Carnegie Hall.

calendarQuote.quote: …experienced with countless and beautiful compositional techniques.

pressGrid.quote: Tellian dissected the athletic, 'Paganini-esque' score to extract its essence: the emotional and pianistic tone that had not existed before Chopin.
Kiron Atom Tellian belongs to the rare breed of pianists who caress the piano, whose fingers lovingly glide over the keyboard, drawing out infinite nuances.
Starting with a concise theme, impressively presented by Tellian, to culminate in a ferocious finale which was rewarded with standing ovations.
His Allemande, Courante and Sarabande all had an expressiveness one most associates with Romanticism. One looks forward to hearing this young man play again.
Tellian's convincing rendition of Ravel's 'Gaspard de la nuit' — probably one of the most difficult works for piano overall — one can only listen, enjoy and wish these young artists all the best.
A fulminant rendition of Chopin's third piano sonata. His ability to play with incredibly nuanced colors and feelings, to connect virtuosity and intimate sensitivity, was extraordinary.
